observations.behavior: Both suppress eager-observer invalidation during speculative writes. Evidence supports unchanged pending observations, no publication on discard, publication after commit, and preserved ordinary updates. A uses Batch.ensure().is_fork; B reads current_batch?.is_fork. The supplied evidence establishes no observable difference between these approaches.
observations.test_coverage: Each passes 1 authored, 2 gold-derived, 8 independent, and 5 native cases, plus syntax checks and build. Both authored tests cover pending/discard/commit visibility, ordinary updates, and conditional dependencies. B additionally changes directly inspected state inside the fork and checks shared-observer unrelated updates before and after discard. A separately checks that an unrelated flush produces no observer notification and displays ordinary alongside eager reads. These are complementary coverage strengths, not demonstrated behavioral differences.
observations.maintenance: Both production changes are small. A reuses Batch but calls ensure; B avoids that call while adding an aliased import midway through the module. Both enlarge an existing asynchronous regression fixture rather than isolating observer tests. These differences do not establish a material maintenance winner.
observations.basis: Tie: both implementations apply and pass identical supplied behavioral suites. No material behavioral advantage is demonstrated.
observations.limits: Conclusions are limited to the frozen diffs and offline results; broader regression freedom is not established. No listed suite was unexecuted. Task renaming was unavailable.

observations.behavior: Both preserve the default 15000-ms wait, configure finite retries, and pass recovery, exhaustion, and non-lock-error checks. A separates post-commit optimization to avoid replaying committed cleanup. B supports extended and named lock diagnostics, but accepting code-less diagnostics risks retrying non-lock errors with identical wording. A instead rejects ambiguous diagnostics, limiting contention recovery on those CLIs.
observations.test_coverage: Both add synthetic contention, retry-bound, configuration, retention, and rollback checks. A additionally targets blocked COMMIT, apply-plan failure propagation, and optimization isolation; B provides broader diagnostic classification cases and deterministic release synchronization. These are source-level coverage differences, not verified execution results.
observations.maintenance: A has simpler classification and clearer post-commit failure reporting. B adds more diagnostic parsing and replays cleanup after optimization failure. Both embed substantial regression harnesses in README documentation.
observations.basis: Tie: both submissions pass the same seven offline behavioral checks and supplied syntax checks. Neither has demonstrated overall behavioral superiority.
observations.limits: Offline checks do not resolve these diagnostic compatibility and post-commit differences. A explicitly says its added harness was not executed; execution of B's added suite is not established. Neither is a demonstrated suite failure. Task renaming was unavailable.

observations.behavior: Both preserve admission checks, guard cleanup failures, roll back partial subscriptions, reconnect through host-owned load listeners, and reference-count host touch subscriptions. Both retain exports and key-delivery logic. Each passed 13 primary checks; both failed the same two cross-origin assertions on WebKit/Mobile Safari, also reported as reference failures—not demonstrated candidate-specific regressions.
observations.test_coverage: Both add targeted cross-origin reconnection, synchronous diagonal cancellation, and host/iframe touch-reopening tests. B additionally exercises child-initiated navigation without src mutation, inaccessible-frame unmount cleanup, and returned-document typing/focus ownership. A tests diagonal cancellation after reload and repeated touch after explicitly hiding controls. These are source-level coverage differences, not verified passing results.
observations.maintenance: A separates host subscriptions into their own effect and consistently guards focus callbacks against stale documents, but repeats listener-registration bookkeeping. B centralizes registration and captures removal methods before navigation, reducing repetition, while keeping host and frame orchestration in one effect. Neither establishes a decisive maintenance advantage.
